name: Domain research and planning
summary: Domain knowledge base, 135 canonical invariants, 500-feature list, Kyle's rulings, tech stack.

name: Schema at parity with the invariants
summary: Close the 80 open invariants in seven waves. Wave 1 landed as v5.4.2-19. Kyle's 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15 answers unblock tax, franchise fees, the PGA billing side and waves 4, 6 and 7. Wave 2: v5.4.2-22 (periods, close snapshot, GL mapping, aging) landed 2026-10-16. v5.4.2-23 (cash: reversals, positions, per-line application, overpayment credits) was mirrored 2026-11-04 after ten review rounds. v5.4.2-27 (a credit applied to a bounced payment's shortfall, recorded; AC-44) went next, ahead of v5.4.2-24 (unmatched cash, agency pledges): Ryan settled two calls on 2026-11-05 (a refund that comes back after its shortfall was paid waits until the repayment is undone; an undo off a credit since escheated is carried into a new credit). Round 2 is reviewed (Fable ready; Opus and Codex not yet, one fix each, both settled by rule); round 3 is next. -27 is one patch the 10-29 estimate did not count. Wave 3 started while waiting: v5.4.2-25 (disputes: the dispute law and tariff rule family, the dispute record, the readers) and v5.4.2-26 (collections decisions: every notice, late fee, disconnect and referral cites a recorded decision; field verification with supervisor overrides) are drafted and tested; both go to review after -23 r3. From 2026-10-29 the schema runs as two parallel streams, each in its own clone: money and collections (-23 to -26, enrollments, notices, new rule types) and rates, meters and places (small fixes, tax and franchise, the gas-cost billing side, zones and factors, read ownership, dated history). The cross-tenant link fix and the version check on every record run last. Rates stream: v5.4.2-28 (small fixes: the state-agency time zone, dated rider dependencies, four-decimal rates) was reviewed ready by all three on round 2 and mirrored 2026-11-04, ahead of the money patches (parity 81 of 135 after it). v5.4.2-29 (every Texas county and its time zone, loaded once as shared data; Ryan 2026-11-04, data only) was mirrored 2026-11-05 after three rounds (Codex found a re-apply defect on round 2; all three ready on round 3); parity unchanged at 85 of 135. Tax and franchise fees are split in three: v5.4.2-30 (the utility's tax rows keyed to places, required taxability, a per-charge late-penalty base, exemptions per service, rates in percent, places as known at a past instant, a state agency's basis) is drafted (round 0, its battery 80 of 80) with older tests to port before review; -31 (franchise fees) waits on Kyle's answer on the franchise base (K-15); -32 loads the Texas cities and districts with the Comptroller's rates.
basis: Counted 2026-10-29: the 56 open invariants grouped into about 15 patches after v5.4.2-23, 24 / 47 / 91 working days in one stream (per-patch days judged from -19 to -23: one a day for the early patches, 12 days and counting for -23). Run as two streams on separate tables (money; rates, meters, places), about half each, plus the two all-table patches last and a week of coordination: 5.5 / 9 / 15 weeks from 2026-10-14. In one stream it would be 7 / 12 / 20.5.

name: Scenarios and testing strategy
summary: Write the 200-390 scenarios the core must pass, have Kyle check the numbers, and choose how they become tests.
basis: Claude drafts at schema pace; the limit is Kyle checking the dollar figures and the 200-390 scenario count. Runs beside P1 from 2026-10-29 (Ryan relaxed the gate's order between steps 1 and 2): families already at parity first; cash, disputes and collections after -23, -25 and -26 mirror; the coverage audit last, once P1 is done.

name: Core build plan
summary: Break the C# core into ordered build phases, each with its scenarios as the finish line. Choose the launch feature set.
basis: Judgment: one planning document plus the launch-feature cut.

name: Platform foundation
summary: AWS environments, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, staff login, the .NET solution, and database access that sets the tenant on every connection.
basis: Judgment at AI pace; depends on the login and hosting decisions. Starts when the schema reaches parity and frees two session slots (Ryan supervises about three at once).

name: Core billing engine (C#)
summary: The billing engine and API, built in sub-phases planned in P3. Each sub-phase finishes when its scenarios pass.
basis: Schema pace used as the stand-in (no C# written yet). Re-measure after the first core sub-phase.

name: Frontend hardening and integration
summary: Take the prototype (36 screens on made-up data) to production: real login, roles, the generated API client, error states, accessibility.
basis: Judgment at AI pace; runs alongside the core once the API exists.

name: Integrations
summary: The outside systems a utility cannot run without. Vendors depend on the first customer's contracts.
basis: Judgment at AI pace; generic adapters only, vendor-specific work happens during onboarding.

name: Test data and release testing
summary: A synthetic utility with a year of history, end-to-end tests, and a full billing-run load test. The fixtures are built from P2 onward; this phase is the final pass.
basis: Judgment: final pass, since fixtures are built during P2 and P5.

name: Security and operations readiness
summary: Backups and disaster recovery, monitoring, an outside penetration test, incident runbooks, and SOC 2 groundwork.
basis: Calendar-bound: the outside penetration test and recovery drills are booked with vendors.

name: First customer: conversion and setup
summary: Starts at the ready-to-onboard date. Convert the customer's data from the old system, load their tariffs and ordinances, and train their staff.
basis: Calendar-bound: the customer staff and old-system vendor set the pace.

name: Parallel billing runs
summary: Bill the customer's real cycles on both systems and reconcile every difference. 2 to 4 monthly cycles.
basis: Calendar-bound: two to four of the customer's monthly billing cycles.

name: Go-live and stabilization
summary: Cut over, then close support for the first live billing cycles.
